How Far Above Its Mode a Restricted Fit Stopped

Source: R/restricted.R
restricted_mode_error.Rd

Computes \(\tfrac12 g'K^{-1}g\) over the free coordinates of a restricted fit, which is the decrease of the penalized objective that a Newton step from the point returned by statmod_restrict() would predict, in log-likelihood units.

Usage

restricted_mode_error(score, information, at)

Arguments

score

The restricted fit's score, all coordinates.

information

Its penalized information, all coordinates.

at

The position of the held coordinate.

Value

A single number, or NA where the score on the free coordinates is not finite, where there is no free coordinate, or where the information on the free coordinates cannot be inverted.

Details

inner_mode_error() computes the same quantity inside a search; here it is applied to a restricted fit. The inner optimizer's flag records whether a stopping rule fired, which is a boolean about a threshold on a score whose size depends on the model, whereas whether a point is at its mode is a matter of distance and has a natural scale. A stopping rule reads a change in the objective and this quantity reads the point, so the two need not agree, and the print method of StatmodTest() reads the mode error and not the flag.

The held coordinate is excluded because it is not free: its score is the quantity that Rao's statistic reads, and it does not vanish under the restriction.

See also

mode_error_limit(), the limit against which it is read, and inner_mode_error(), the same reading inside a search.
